doc.title: Percy Heath — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Opening of the Smithsonian interview at Heath's Montauk home
summary: Holley introduces the session at Percy Heath's home in Montauk on July 23, 2001; Heath jokes about the date and asks to be called Percy.

story.theme_name: Starting the tape: names, dates and places
story.community_name: Opening the interview: introductions, date and place

blocks.x: Funding for the Smithsonian Jazz Oral History Program NEA Jazz Master interview was provided by the National Endowment for the Arts.
Interviewer: Eugene Holley with recording engineer Sven Aboe Institution Description: Transcript, 72 pp.

Okay, my name is Eugene Holley. I am here with engineer Sven Abow for the Smithsonian Jazz Oral History Project at the home of Mr. Percy Leroy Heath Jr. in Montauk, Long Island on Monday, July the 23rd. Thank you Mr. Heath.
Two thousand and one, and you can believe that.
Two thousand and one, two thousand and one, and it’s not a space odyssey.
Mr. Heath, I think I can speak on behalf of everyone here, it is such a great honor and a privilege to be talking with you, and thank you. Let me just say that right off the bat, if I can say that.
You can say that right off the bat and you can say Percy.
